estimated_overhead.memory: one frozenset per engine per Propagation (<= horizon ints) and one small set per sweep; negligible against the measured tracemalloc peaks
estimated_overhead.source: timeit of two frozenset.isdisjoint calls on a 7-value tuple (measured 128 ns) against 619 ns for the current comprehension on the same input

gate.required: plausible >= 20% reduction of TOTAL fixed-work compile-call time after overhead (fixed-work ratio <= 0.80)

scan_cost_model_least_squares.source: timers_split exclusive seconds vs count-mode counters

mechanism.cache: none across calls (S_e is a per-Propagation constant derived from the domain; nothing crosses programs)
mechanism.class: representation-level reduction of repeated domain work (plan section 4)
mechanism.description: Per Propagation, precompute per engine the frozenset S_e of cycles full from fixed issues alone (base >= limit); per sweep, derive from the singles map the set Dyn_e of cycles made full by selected singletons. For a non-singleton op of engine e, full is empty iff its domain is disjoint from S_e | Dyn_e (C-level isdisjoint); only then is the scan skipped. Otherwise the ORIGINAL comprehension runs unchanged, so full, the EF certificates, their order and kept are identical.
mechanism.exactness_argument: c is full iff base(e,c) + n_singles(e,c) >= limit; if n_singles = 0 this is base >= limit, i.e. c in S_e; if n_singles > 0, (e,c) is a singles key and c is in Dyn_e iff the same inequality holds. Hence F_e = S_e | Dyn_e exactly.

prediction.note: a prediction from measured counts and a measured cost model, not a guaranteed speedup

why_no_other_mechanism: Every single component has a zero-cost ceiling above 0.80 (bounds 0.805, rule-2 scan 0.819, address support 0.846, precedence 0.865): even deleting one entirely at no cost cannot reach a 20% total saving.

Only the whole times_fixpoint (precedence + rule 2) has a ceiling below 0.80 (0.582). A change-driven reformulation of that fixpoint is the worklist mechanism already measured at 4.8% (next_round_20260925 ENGINEERING_DECISION.json); the plan forbids assuming another worklist wins.
Caches are not justified: exact repeated inputs within one domain are 0.33% of times_fixpoint calls, 2.6% of compulsory_peak calls, 0.67% of prune calls and 2.1% of addresses_fixpoint calls.
The plan forbids trying several mechanisms until one looks favourable; no second proposal is written.
